implement.approach: Regression-first: the new shipping-path suite apps/mobile/__tests__/w08ManageAccountDeletion.test.tsx was committed before each implementation step (dfe9505a principal suite; fc5e137b teardown; 74a88105 stale 409; 08e05abc/77cf8f8d/58df91b6 superseded; 881f46a4 clock rollback; bd2d15b2 account switch) and shown to fail on BASE_SHA (46/50) and, for this round's additions, on the previous candidate (7/7). ManageAccountScreen now drives a durable AccountDeletionFlow from src/account/deletion.ts that builds the deletionOperation foundation (SQLite journal + Keychain capability vault + deletionOperationTransport over fetchNoRedirect) bound to the active owner and API origin: request -> secure -> review pause -> confirm -> observe/poll -> receipt -> cleanup, with one journal row per operation so remount/retry/relaunch resume the same operationId instead of minting a new request. The UI maps journal phases to honest states (ready / request unknown / confirmation unknown / in progress / rate limited / failed / completed) and calls onDeleted (completeAccountDeletion) only from a server-verified receipt. Adversary findings fixed at root cause: journal rows parse independently (owner B unaffected by owner A's corrupt row, owner A held); the verified receipt is journaled before the Keychain seal so a refused seal or an expired status window still completes from the journal; unmount invalidates the presentation so a late poll reply is dropped; flows are cached per foundation and in-flight jobs are tracked so re-entry reports unresolved-same-account and the late reply completes once; a 409 refusal is honoured only until its Retry-After; superseded is a nothing-deleted terminal; pacing deadlines are clamped against the foundation's own maximum wait so a wall-clock rollback cannot stretch backoff or the review pause; an account switch over a sent confirmation is described as unresolved for the earlier account, never 'start again', and no poll goes out under the new bearer.

residual_risks: The adversary-style relaunch after a Keychain-refused receipt seal is covered by the official suite (onDeleted runs once, for the deleted owner). A temporary exploratory test during this session observed completeAccountDeletion being called twice across initial completion + relaunch in one contrived sequence (complete, then remount the same screen and re-open the sheet before sign-out settles); that exploratory file was removed and the scenario is not in the official suite — recommend the adversary probe it. completeAccountDeletion in authStore is itself idempotent for the same owner, so the user-visible effect would be a repeated sign-out/cleanup, not data loss or a false deletion.

Pacing clamp (deletionPacingCapMs: 60s for local backoff, 24h for server in_progress/rate_limited waits) is a client-side bound: a server Retry-After longer than 24h is honoured only up to 24h before the UI offers to ask the server again; the server remains the source of truth and simply re-refuses if still pacing.
Native Keychain/SQLite behaviour is exercised through Jest doubles only; no iOS device/simulator run was performed (TypeScript-only scope, Mac runner reserved for the coordinator).
